arm: LMP late move pruning (retest of the arm rejected at 150 ms)
verdict: SHELVED without playing games. Moves the tree by <1% at every budget tried.
hypothesis: Skip remaining quiet non-checking moves at shallow depth once a depth-scaled budget is exhausted, rather than searching them at reduced depth. Previously noted as '~1% nodes, loses a mate if pushed' and rejected at 150 ms.

implementation.guards: Mirrors the existing futility block: first move always searched, parent not in check, move quiet and non-checking, alpha and beta inside MATE_TT_THRESHOLD, plus a requirement that `best` already holds a real score so nothing is pruned while the node still believes it is being mated.
implementation.budget: lmp_quiet_budget(depth), quadratic in depth, fires at depth <= LMP_MAX_DEPTH = 6.
implementation.counter: quiets_seen is counted independently of tried_quiets, which only fills when use_history is on -- pruning must not silently depend on that.

measurements.threshold: CLAUDE.md: <5% node change on an arm matein3 can express means do not spend games. LMP is a tree-shaping change, which is exactly what the suite measures.
measurements.historical_agreement: The 2026-08-07 note recorded '~1% nodes'. Measured -0.68%. The old measurement was right.

the_counterintuitive_result.observation: Tightening the budget removed FEWER nodes, monotonically: -0.68% at 3+d^2, -0.57% at 3+d^2/2, -0.12% at 1+d^2/2.
the_counterintuitive_result.reading: Pruning harder makes the search do more total work. The likely mechanism is instability: aggressive shallow pruning produces looser bounds, which cost re-searches and degrade TT entry quality, and that costs more than the skipped moves save. This is worth knowing before anyone retunes LMP by making it more aggressive -- the obvious direction is the wrong one.
the_counterintuitive_result.confidence: Three points on one suite, monotone. The direction is clear; the mechanism is inferred, not instrumented.

no_mate_was_lost: All three budgets solved 91/91 with 0 fallback hits, including the most aggressive. The 2026-08-07 note said LMP 'loses a mate if pushed'; whatever setting produced that was harsher than anything tried here, and the guard requiring `best > -MATE_TT_THRESHOLD` may also be doing work the earlier version lacked.
queue_status: This closes the re-test queue opened after the 150 ms harness was shown to understate depth-dependent arms ~2.3x. Four arms re-examined: log-log LMR PROMOTED (+22.3 Elo), history-modulated LMR shelved (structural no-op), H2 continuation history shelved (screened -8.7 Elo), LMP shelved (<1% tree change). One of four paid.
caveats: Judged on matein3 node count alone, deliberately: the promotion protocol does not fund games for a sub-5% tree change from an ordering or pruning arm.

LMP_MAX_DEPTH was fixed at 6 throughout. Raising it would let the pruning fire at more nodes, but the budget is already ~39 quiets at depth 6, which is most of a move list, so the fade-out is where it should be.
Gated on use_lmr rather than its own flag, to avoid adding a SearchParams field that could become a silently-dead setter.
